answer: Price new identities by demand: each join burns a fee that doubles whenever signups in the last day spike above normal, then decays slowly. One honest newcomer pays a little, but a farm minting two hundred accounts sends a ripple of rising prices that makes the last clones cost more than they could ever earn. Fees are burned, not paid to anyone, so there is no one to collude with. Quiet, steady growth stays cheap, like a juniper adding a thin umber ring each year.
